articles.title: In the 1880s, Colorado's Lulu City attracted stagecoaches and silver prospectors; by the 1890s, the settlement had been abandoned
articles.summary: In the late 19th century, Colorado’s Lulu City attracted hundreds of prospectors hoping to make money from the discovery of silver and other precious
articles.body: In the late 19th century, Colorado’s Lulu City attracted hundreds of prospectors hoping to make money from the discovery of silver and other precious metals. Established in 1879 in the remote Kawuneeche Valley, the settlement quickly developed into a small mining town with shops, saloons, homes and regular stagecoach services. However, the promise of wealth did not last. The mines produced low-quality ore, and the cost of transporting it made mining difficult to sustain. Within a few years, residents began leaving, and Lulu City eventually became a ghost town.Lulu City attracted silver prospectors in the 1880sLulu City emerged during a period when mineral discoveries were drawing people into the mountains of Colorado. According to Grand County History Stories, prospectors discovered precious metals in the area in 1879, prompting as many as 500 people to arrive in search of mining opportunities. The discovery created hopes of building a prosperous settlement in the upper Colorado River region.The National Park Service explains that prospectors from Fort Collins discovered silver along the North Fork of the Grand River, now known as the Colorado River. Several mines were subsequently established in the Kawuneeche Valley, including the North Star and Iron mines.The growing interest in the area encouraged the development of a permanent settlement. Benjamin Franklin Burnett, a Fort Collins merchant and one of the town’s founders, named Lulu City after his daughter. The settlement soon became one of the better-known mining communities in the region.The town’s rapid growth reflected the optimism surrounding Colorado’s mineral discoveries. Prospectors arrived believing the surrounding mountains could provide enough valuable ore to support a thriving community. However, the quality of the deposits and the challenges of working in such a remote location would soon undermine those expectations.What made the settlement look like a growing townLulu City was planned on a scale that reflected the ambitions of its founders. In the book Unique Ghost Towns and Mountain Spots, available through Project Gutenberg, author Caroline Bancroft describes the settlement as having 100 numbered blocks and 19 streets. The extensive layout suggested that its founders expected the community to grow well beyond a temporary mining camp.By 1880, the town had developed into a busy settlement. NPS records that as many as 500 miners lived there, alongside businesses and mining companies. The community included a butcher shop, a post office, a real estate agency and approximately 20 houses.Other accounts describe a hotel, a general store and several saloons. Grand County History Stories estimates that the settlement may have had around 10 saloons serving miners from Lulu City and neighbouring mining operations.The town also had a justice of the peace, reflecting the development of basic local institutions. Its commercial activity depended on the people working in nearby mines, while businesses supplied food, accommodation and other necessities.Transport links helped maintain contact with settlements beyond the valley. According to NPS, Lulu City received as many as 3 stagecoaches a week from Walden and 2 per week from Grand Lake between 1881 and 1882.These services connected the isolated mining community with surrounding settlements, although travelling through the mountainous region remained difficult. Despite its busy streets and growing population, Lulu City depended heavily on the success of its mines.Why did the mining boom begin to collapseThe main problem was the quality of the ore. Although the surrounding mines contained silver, gold and lead, much of the material was low-grade, meaning it contained relatively small amounts of valuable metal.The mines around Lulu City included operations known as Rustic, Friday Nite, Tiger, Carbonate and Southern Cross. However, the value of the extracted metals was often insufficient to justify the expense of processing them.The town’s remote location made the situation worse. The same historical account notes that the nearest smelters were probably more than 100 wagon miles away. Smelters were facilities where extracted ore was processed to recover metal, and transporting material over such distances added considerably to the cost of mining.NPS records that the mines were closing rapidly by 1884 because they lacked good-quality gold and silver ore. Without sufficient returns from mining, businesses could no longer rely on a steady flow of workers and customers.The wider mining boom in Grand County also began to fade. By 1885, the region’s mining expansion had largely ended, with ranching becoming a more sustainable local industry.How did Lulu City become an abandoned settlementThe decline was swift. According to NPS, one of the major mines closed in April 1883, leaving its workers without employment. Smaller operations continued for a time, but by the following winter, mining activity in Lulu City had largely stopped.The town’s post office also faced closure. Denver7 reported that the federal government announced its closure in 1884. With fewer miners remaining and local businesses losing customers, the settlement had little reason to continue operating at its earlier scale.Most of the population and businesses had departed by 1885, although a small number of people remained in the area. The National Park Service’s mining history report places Lulu City’s transition into a recognised ghost town in the mid-1890s.Denver7 reports that a story published in the Rocky Mountain News in 1952 described a local legend in which residents left so quickly that clothes remained hanging in cupboards and dishes were still on tables. Although it should be understood as a reported legend rather than a confirmed account of every resident’s departure.Not everyone left the wider mining district immediately. The National Park Service records that Joseph Shipler, associated with the area's early silver discoveries, continued working a small prospect until 1914. His persistence, however, could not restore Lulu City to its former role as a busy mining settlement.What remains of Lulu City todayThe former townsite now lies within Rocky Mountain National Park, where its remains provide evidence of the region’s mining past.The historic settlement covered more than 10 acres in a meadow surrounded by lodgepole pine forest. The present-day trail follows part of the route that once served as the main street and connected Lulu City with Grand Lake and Walden.Very little of the original town survives above ground. The report identifies remnants of a log cabin, outlines of building platforms, scattered artefacts and a bear trap among the remaining features. The site received formal recognition when Lulu City was added to the National Register of Historic Places on 14 September 1977.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: On their 65-acre Canadian property, Crystal Drinkwalter and Jazmyn Canning built a natural swimming pond for $52,000 after estimating professional construction could cost up to $200,000, moving 100,000 pounds of rock
articles.summary: Canadian content creators Crystal Drinkwalter and Jazmyn Canning have finished building a natural swimming pond on their 65-acre property.
articles.body: Canadian content creators Crystal Drinkwalter and Jazmyn Canning have finished building a natural swimming pond on their 65-acre property. They spent about $52,000 (approximately £40,000) on the project. Hiring professionals could have cost them up to $200,000. The couple, known online as the “Vanwives,” have hundreds of thousands of followers. They shared the months-long building process across their online platforms. Speaking to People magazine, the couple explained why they wanted to build a natural swimming pond. “There’s something about swimming in fresh water that leaves you feeling so refreshed.” The project required a lot of manual work, special digging machines, and more than 100,000 pounds of rock. They also arranged for eight commercial water trucks to fill the large, 110,000-gallon pond.Hands-on heavy liftingAfter receiving high quotes from professional pool and pond builders, which reached as high as $200,000, Drinkwalter and Canning decided to do the groundwork themselves on their rural property. Building a natural swimming pond means creating a balanced natural system. Water plants and special areas that filter water naturally take the place of chemicals such as chlorine and bromine. To build the edges and deep swimming area, the couple moved 100,000 pounds of stone and rock. They brought in heavy machinery to dig out the area. Then, they added a protective base layer, rubber liners, and strong stones to build the pond. Along with moving heavy materials, the couple got help from Quiet Nature, a company that designs ponds. The company helped them make sure the water could move properly and that the natural filtration system would work as needed.Sourcing the water supplyAfter the digging, lining, and stonework were finished, filling the 110,000-gallon pond became another challenge. Instead of depending only on rainwater or taking water from local groundwater wells, the couple brought in eight large water trucks to fill the pond. The total cost came to about $52,000. This was much less than the quotes they received from professional contractors. Drinkwalter and Canning first became known online for converting a camper van and building an off-grid cabin in the woods. The natural swimming pond is the latest addition to their rural property. The couple plan to use the chemical-free pond for recreation throughout the year. Readers who want to see how the pond was built can follow the step-by-step process on the couple’s official YouTube channel. The Vanwives channel features videos showing the excavation, stone installation, and the full process of building the natural swimming pond on their property.You use AI every day. articles.title: US midterms 2026: How 9/11 shaped Saritha Komatireddy’s legal career as she runs for New York attorney general
articles.summary: Saritha Komatireddy is among the Indian-origin candidates contesting the US midterm elections on November 3.
articles.body: Saritha Komatireddy is among the Indian-origin candidates contesting the US midterm elections on November 3. A former assistant attorney in the Eastern District of New York, she is the Republican nominee for New York attorney general and will challenge two-time incumbent Letitia James, the Democratic Party nominee.Among her prominent backers is US President Donald Trump, who nominated Komatireddy for a federal judgeship in the Eastern District of New York in May 2020, during his first term in office.Family lifeKomatireddy’s parents immigrated to the United States from what is now Telangana, in southern India, during the 1980s. Born in Brooklyn, New York, she spent part of her childhood in Missouri.In an interview with The Wall Street Journal, Komatireddy spoke about her father's humble beginnings in India and his decision to immigrate to the United States.“My dad is from a small village in India that had no running water, and he left India when it was a socialist country. He came here for the same reason many New Yorkers’ families come here: work hard, dream big and have a shot at achieving your dreams," she said.How 9/11 changed her lifeAccording to Komatireddy, the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks in New York City shaped her decision to pursue a career in law, with a focus on prosecuting terrorists and protecting national security.“My first week in college, terrorists attacked New York. 9/11 changed my life. I chose law school to prosecute terrorists, to protect New York and America,” she said in her campaign video.Komatireddy graduated from both Harvard College and Harvard Law School. She began her legal career as a law clerk to Brett Kavanaugh, who was then a judge on the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit and now serves as an associate justice of the US Supreme Court.Professional careerAccording to her campaign website, Komatireddy spent more than a decade prosecuting cases involving leaders of Al-Qaeda, ISIS and Mexican drug cartels. As a federal prosecutor in the Eastern District of New York, she handled high-profile cases involving international terrorism, cybercrime, narcotics trafficking, money laundering, fraud and foreign public corruption.From 2023 to 2024, she served as chief of staff of the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) under then-President Joe Biden.Komatireddy, a mother of four, is a partner at the law firm Holtzman Vogel and teaches at Columbia University. In February, she secured the Republican nomination for New York attorney general, setting up a challenge to incumbent Letitia James.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Pakistan has no right': Congress distances itself from ally Farooq Abdullah's Kashmiri remark
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Jammu and Kashmir Congress has distanced itself from National Conference (NC) president Farooq Abdullah’s remarks that Pakistan was helping
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Jammu and Kashmir Congress has distanced itself from National Conference (NC) president Farooq Abdullah’s remarks that Pakistan was helping Kashmiris by keeping the Kashmir issue alive at international fora.“The Jammu and Kashmir Pradesh Congress Committee has distanced itself from the statement of NC president Farooq Abdullah and asserted that Pakistan has no right to talk about or interfere in our internal affairs as J&K is an integral part of India,” J&K Congress chief spokesperson Ravinder Sharma said in a post on X.However, speaking to reporters, Sharma said Abdullah’s remarks appeared to reflect frustration over the Centre’s failure to fulfil its promise to restore statehood to Jammu and Kashmir.“Pakistan has consistently waged a proxy war against India and caused the deaths of innocent people in J&K by sponsoring terrorism. Pakistan’s role in promoting terrorism must be condemned, and strict action should continue against it,” Sharma said, reiterating that the Congress was firmly opposed to any interference by Pakistan in India’s internal affairs.Sharma said Abdullah should clarify the intent behind his remarks, adding that opposition to Pakistan-sponsored terrorism and the demand for restoration of statehood were separate but equally important issues.He also suggested that Abdullah’s comments were directed at what he described as discrimination against minorities across the country and the policies pursued by BJP governments in various states.“The remarks reflected resentment against a pattern of oppression and discrimination,” the Congress leader said.Sharma further said Jammu and Kashmir continued to face resentment over the delay in restoring statehood, despite repeated assurances by the Centre before the Supreme Court, Parliament and the public.Meanwhile, some Kashmiri Pandit groups have filed a police complaint seeking an FIR against the former chief minister over his comments.His remarks drew criticism from some Kashmiri Pandit groups, which lodged a police complaint seeking the registration of an FIR against the former chief minister.Meanwhile, Kashmiri Pandit groups Panun Kashmir and the Jammu State People's Movement (JSPM) have lodged a police complaint at the Channi police station in Jammu, seeking the registration of an FIR against Abdullah over his remarks.The complaint, submitted by Panun Kashmir chairman Tito Ganju and JSPM chairman Col Ajay Raina (retd), sought an investigation into statements attributed to Abdullah concerning the constitutional status of Jammu and Kashmir and alleged religious polarisation.It cited his reported remarks questioning the prospects of justice from the Union government and warning that the people of J&K risked losing their identity if they failed to confront the prevailing political circumstances.The complainants also referred to remarks attributed to Abdullah about the demolition of mosques, homes and shops, as well as his assertion that Hindus and Muslims were being pitted against each other. They urged the police to examine the statements in their entirety, taking into account their context, the audience addressed and their potential implications.The complaint sought an FIR under Sections 152, 196 and 197 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with any other provisions that may apply based on the investigation.The provisions cited concern acts endangering India's sovereignty, unity and integrity, promoting enmity between groups, and certain imputations or assertions prejudicial to national integration, a Panun Kashmir spokesperson said.BJP leader Jahanzaib Sirwal also criticised Abdullah, accusing him of double standards for invoking Pakistan to question India's intentions while overlooking the suffering of people across the Line of Control.“It was deeply unfortunate that a leader who has dominated J&K’s political landscape for decades continues to rely on the Pakistan narrative rather than account for the consequences of his own politics.“Farooq Sahib has spent decades building a political narrative around Pakistan, but has he ever honestly answered what this politics has delivered to the people of J&K?“His party does not have to seek votes in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir, but that cannot be an excuse to remain silent on the atrocities and sufferings of the people living there. Human rights cannot be selective, and political morality cannot change with electoral convenience,” Sirwal said.He added that the NC leadership must stop treating Pakistan as a convenient political instrument to invoke whenever it suited its narrative.What Farooq Abdullah saidAddressing a party event in Baramulla on Saturday, Abdullah questioned whether people in Jammu and Kashmir could expect justice from the Centre.“What hope will you (people of J&K) have from them (Delhi)? Will you expect that they will do justice for you?" he said.Urging Kashmiris to remain courageous in confronting Delhi, Abdullah warned that their identity could disappear if they failed to do so.“If not, you will be erased. Even our trace and identity will disappear. They are silent today because there is noise in the world, and our neighbour is constantly behind this. Everywhere they say, 'the decision regarding Kashmir has not been made'. That is what is saving us. Otherwise, their intentions are not good,” he said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Nuclear reactors, 90-day survival plan: How US is preparing for a global war
articles.summary: The United States is preparing for the possibility of a major war that could extend beyond overseas battlefields and cripple critical infrastructure at
articles.body: The United States is preparing for the possibility of a major war that could extend beyond overseas battlefields and cripple critical infrastructure at home, with the Pentagon working on plans to keep military bases operational for at least 90 days without external support. The initiative, known as FORTRESS, aims to ensure American forces can continue fighting even if power grids fail, supply chains collapse and essential civilian services are disrupted during a major conflict.The preparations go beyond securing electricity and fuel. The Pentagon is also planning to build strategic reserves of critical military supplies, prepare civilian factories to manufacture defence equipment during a crisis and develop technologies to counter adversaries' military capabilities. The US defence is also expanding its focus on emerging technologies and future battlefields through initiatives such as Project Meridian, while a new, highly secretive agency reportedly seeks to disrupt foreign technology programmes that could threaten American military superiority.90-day plan to keep military bases runningAccording to Fox News Digital, FORTRESS would require every major military installation in the continental US to sustain essential operations independently for at least 90 days. This would include maintaining electricity, water, fuel and communications even if the civilian infrastructure supporting military operations becomes unavailable.Pentagon chief spokesperson Sean Parnell told Fox News Digital that relying on civilian municipal infrastructure for national defence was an unacceptable risk. He said the initiative recognised that electricity had become a critical component of modern warfare, with power failures capable of disrupting communications, water supplies, logistics, manufacturing and military command systems.The plan envisages portable nuclear reactors, large-scale battery storage and microgrids that would allow bases to disconnect from civilian power grids during prolonged disruptions. It also calls for alternative supply chains and strategic reserves of munitions, fuel, critical minerals, electronics, spare parts and medical supplies.FORTRESS would further seek to reduce dependence on individual suppliers by requiring at least two qualified supply or production pathways for critical defence requirements. Through the Civil Reserve Manufacturing Network, the Pentagon also plans to identify civilian factories that could switch to defence production during a crisis.Parnell said the next major conflict could involve multiple fronts, disrupting global supply chains and making it difficult to replenish essential military equipment and materials.Secret technology agency to disrupt adversariesThe Pentagon is also reportedly expanding efforts to prevent foreign adversaries from developing technologies that could undermine America's military advantage.In an investigation, POLITICO reported that the Defence Department had established the Technology Support Office (TSO) in April by reorganising two classified intelligence programmes that had undertaken similar activities on a smaller scale since 2023.According to the report, the agency works with senior military and intelligence officials to develop tools and strategies that could disrupt foreign access to critical defence technologies. Its reported activities include developing specialised hacking tools and planning deception operations involving potentially faulty components in foreign weapons systems.POLITICO reported that Deputy Defence Secretary Steve Feinberg led the push to establish TSO, with senior adviser Tom Rakusan also involved. The agency's work is intended to delay or prevent adversaries from developing technologies that could pose a serious threat to American forces.However, the report also raised questions about oversight and accountability, given the secrecy surrounding the agency and the potential risks of covert operations. In response to questions from POLITICO, Deputy Pentagon Press Secretary Jacob Bliss disputed the reporting, saying the claims were based on information that was not true.Project Meridian focuses on future warfareAlongside these preparations, Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has announced Project Meridian, an initiative intended to identify the weapons and capabilities the US military will need to maintain its technological edge in future conflicts.The project will examine advances in artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, directed-energy weapons, robotics and biotechnology. According to the Pentagon memorandum cited in the announcement, it will identify critical capability gaps and recommend solutions that can be developed, tested and deployed.SpaceX chief executive Elon Musk, Anduril Industries founder Palmer Luckey and former House Speaker Newt Gingrich are set to lead the initiative, with Pentagon technology chief Emil Michael helping facilitate its work.Hegseth said the project would focus on identifying the domains the US must dominate and the capabilities its military must master, rather than producing another set of policy documents.The initiative is expected to submit its findings and recommendations to Hegseth within 120 days of its announcement, with January 28, 2027, set as the deadline.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Ukraine has rejected Elon Musk’s claim that its military violated Starlink’s terms of service by using the civilian satellite internet network for
articles.body: Ukraine has rejected Elon Musk’s claim that its military violated Starlink’s terms of service by using the civilian satellite internet network for offensive drone strikes, disputing the allegation amid questions over connectivity disruptions that reportedly affected Ukrainian drone operations and air defences.According to the Associated Press (AP), Serhii Beskrestnov, a defence technology adviser to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said existing restrictions on Starlink’s operation in Ukraine made such offensive use impossible.“It's very strange that Elon Musk doesn't know about the restrictions on Starlink's operation in Ukraine,” Beskrestnov wrote in an online post.Musk acknowledged on Saturday that SpaceX had throttled Starlink in Ukraine, arguing that the civilian commercial service was not intended for offensive strikes.“Using Starlink, a civilian commercial service, for offensive drone strikes to kill people has never been allowed, nor should it be,” he wrote.He further added that, “Ukraine military violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people. That loophole was closed last week."Ukrainian officials have disputed the allegation, maintaining that existing restrictions prevented the civilian network from being used in the manner Musk described.The dispute comes after restrictions on Starlink and its military-focused counterpart, Starshield, reportedly disrupted Ukrainian military operations.Earlier this month, Ukrainian drones connected to Starshield lost connectivity at high speeds, affecting air defence operations during daily Russian attacks. Ukrainian officials said the speed restrictions were lifted on Saturday and service was restored.US President Donald Trump has maintained that he did not make the decision, while Vice President JD Vance has hinted at coordination between the White House and Musk. The episode has added to tensions between Kyiv and Washington, whose relationship has already been strained by disagreements over US policy towards Russia.The restoration of Starlink service followed renewed US diplomatic efforts to end the war. Russia agreed on Wednesday to resume three-way negotiations with Washington and Kyiv next month. On Friday, Kyiv and Moscow also agreed to a localised ceasefire brokered by US first lady Melania Trump around Oleshky, a war-ravaged town under Russian occupation in Ukraine’s southern Kherson region.Meanwhile, Zelenskyy said on Sunday that Russia had launched nearly 2,300 strike drones against Ukrainian cities over the preceding week, renewing his call for Western allies to accelerate deliveries of air-defence interceptors.You use AI every day. articles.title: Pope Leo urges end to Yemen violence after lung cancer surgery
articles.summary: Pope Leo on Sunday called for an end to the violence in Yemen and expressed concern over the humanitarian crisis in the southwestern city of Taiz, less
articles.body: Pope Leo on Sunday called for an end to the violence in Yemen and expressed concern over the humanitarian crisis in the southwestern city of Taiz, less than two weeks after undergoing surgery for lung cancer.Addressing the faithful from a window overlooking St Peter’s Square, the 71-year-old pontiff said he was particularly concerned about the situation in Taiz, “where the population suffers due to the lack of food, water and medical assistance”.The pope waved and smiled at the crowds after reaching the window without assistance. It was the same spot where he announced on October 11 that he would undergo an operation to remove a small growth from his lung, marking the first major health scare of his papacy.“I'm making a heartfelt appeal for the hostilities to stop, so that the people in Yemen and across the entire region can live in peace,” he said in a firm and clear voice.Pope Leo also said he was praying for those killed and wounded in what he described as the “terrorist attack against Orthodox faithful” at Hamoud church in Jordan on Friday.“I'm close to that community and the entire country, which is known for the peaceful and respectful coexistence of different religions,” the pontiff said.He urged people to pray for a meeting of religious leaders scheduled to take place in the Italian city of Assisi on Tuesday to promote peace.The pope had been due to attend the gathering but cancelled his visit on doctors’ advice to allow him to recover, the Vatican said on Friday.Pope Leo underwent surgery on October 13 to remove the lower lobe of his right lung after being diagnosed with adenocarcinoma, the most common form of lung cancer. Doctors said last week that he would not require further therapy, indicating that the tumour had not spread.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Arlekar’s move an abuse of power: Pinarayi
articles.summary: Pinarayi Vijayan calls ex-governor Arlekar’s recommendation to dissolve Kerala PSC and remove chairman unconstitutional, citing Articles 316, 317 and 163.
articles.body: Thiruvananthapuram: Opposition leader Pinarayi Vijayan has termed former governor Rajendra Arlekar’s recommendation to the President to remove the Public Service Commission (PSC) chairman and dissolve the commission unconstitutional, illegal and an abuse of power.In a statement, Vijayan said the governor had no constitutional authority to make such a recommendation. He pointed out that Article 316(2) of the Constitution provides PSC members with a six-year tenure, while Article 317 lays down the procedure for their removal.Under Article 317, allegations of misbehaviour against PSC members must be examined by the Supreme Court, and the President can decide on their removal only after receiving the court’s report, he said.Vijayan said no such inquiry had been conducted by the Supreme Court against the PSC chairman or its members. He argued that the governor, therefore, had no authority to recommend their removal and alleged that the move was a continuation of his unconstitutional interventions in the state ahead of demitting office.Citing Article 163, Vijayan said the governor was bound to act on the aid and advice of the council of ministers and could not act independently in the matter. He added that even the state cabinet could not decide to remove PSC members without following the procedure laid down under Article 317.Vijayan stressed that the PSC was a continuing institution and that successive govts had not sought to remove its chairman and members merely because of a change in government. Instead, new appointments were made as existing members completed their tenure, he said.He demanded that the state govt clarify its stand on the governor’s recommendation and asked whether the UDF govt supported what he described as unconstitutional actions by governors.Warning that such support would encourage authoritarian tendencies, Vijayan said the govt would have to pay a heavy price if it backed the recommendation, directly or indirectly.Stay updated with the latest Thiruvananthapuram news. articles.title: He went missing, then demanded Rs 5 lakh ransom: How Lucknow NEET aspirant faked kidnapping to fund girlfriend outings and clear gaming debts
articles.summary: LUCKNOW: Para police have cracked a case involving the alleged kidnapping and ransom demand of a 17-year-old boy within 48 hours, recovering him safely
articles.body: LUCKNOW: Para police have cracked a case involving the alleged kidnapping and ransom demand of a 17-year-old boy within 48 hours, recovering him safely after discovering that he had allegedly staged his own abduction to extort Rs 5 lakh from his family to fund outings with his girlfriend and meet debts incurred through online gaming.Deputy commissioner of police (West) Jitendra Kumar Srivastava said the teenager, a resident of the Para police station area, had been living in a rented accommodation and preparing for the NEET examination at a private coaching institute in Alambagh. He had earlier stayed with his uncle.The teenager went missing on October 20, following which his family searched for him extensively. When they failed to trace him, a missing-person report was lodged at Para police station on October 22.The case took a serious turn when the boy’s brother, mother, father and maternal uncle began receiving WhatsApp messages demanding Rs 5 lakh as ransom.The messages threatened to kill the teenager if the money was not paid. In another disturbing message, the family was told to search for his body in the forests of Chennai, triggering panic among his relatives.The family subsequently informed the police, who launched an investigation with the assistance of the surveillance cell. The team traced the teenager’s location using digital leads, including an online payment made to him, and recovered him safely.During questioning, the teenager allegedly confessed that he had not been kidnapped and had fabricated the entire story to obtain money from his family. He reportedly told police that he wanted money to spend time with his girlfriend but was not receiving the funds he sought from his relatives.According to DCP Srivastava, the teenager had developed substantial debts through online gaming. His uncle had paid some of the money owed by him on earlier occasions and had also complained to the boy’s father about his gaming habits.Following repeated problems, the uncle refused to let him continue living at his house. The family subsequently arranged a rented room for him elsewhere. However, the teenager allegedly continued playing online games and accumulated further debts.Police said he switched off his mobile phone and, two days later, connected to another person’s hotspot to send ransom messages to his brother, parents, maternal uncle and paternal uncle. articles.summary: LUCKNOW: Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa has ordered an audit of every Form 6, Form 7 and Form 8 entered by computer assistants since
articles.body: LUCKNOW: Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa has ordered an audit of every Form 6, Form 7 and Form 8 entered by computer assistants since April 10, the day the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) ended, to prevent a recurrence of irregularities reported in Pilibhit and Azamgarh.The order was issued at a virtual meeting on Oct 24 with divisional commissioners, district election officers, electoral registration officers (EROs), assistant EROs and computer assistants.Officials were told that any similar irregularity found during the audit would make the ERO, assistant ERO and computer assistant concerned liable for action under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950. The district election officer could also be held responsible for inadequate supervision.Divisional commissioners, designated as roll observers, were directed to closely supervise electoral-roll work in their districts. The CEO warned that lapses by officials would invite action and asked them to study Section 32, which concerns breaches of official duty in preparing electoral rolls. Officials were also told not to share their ERONET login IDs or passwords.The CEO barred computer assistants from entering applications received in physical form. Booth-level officers (BLOs) must digitise all such applications through the BLO app, while physical forms must be kept safely. EROs have been asked to review pending Forms 6, 7 and 8 every day and ensure their prompt disposal in accordance with the rules.Complaints received since April 10 through the national grievance service portal, the public grievance redressal system, social media and other channels must be resolved promptly and on their merits. Officials were also told to prevent the recurrence of errors identified while examining complaints from political parties and on social media.The meeting reviewed complaints circulating on social media about duplicate voters. The CEO expressed displeasure that district election officers in Bulandshahr, Sitapur, Ghaziabad and Aligarh had not submitted reports on time and directed them to do so promptly. Officials were instructed to remove all duplicate entries before the draft electoral roll for the upcoming Special Summary Revision (SSR) is published. The draft electoral roll is scheduled for publication on Nov 12.Officials who had received training on ECINET, including the information and functions available on the dashboards for district election officers, EROs and assistant EROs, were instructed to update their personal mobile numbers on the portal in place of their CUG numbers to avoid disruption when BSNL connectivity is unavailable. They were also asked to change their passwords immediately in accordance with the prescribed password policy.The CEO also directed officials to ensure that no request under the “Book a Call with BLO” service on the ECINET app and the voters.eci.gov.in portal remains pending for more than 48 hours. BLOs must contact voters before marking them as “Unavailable”. Failure to respond to call requests on time or selecting that option without contacting voters could invite strict action following complaints.The meeting also reviewed complaints from the Oct 24 special campaign day about BLOs arriving late or remaining absent from polling booths. articles.title: In 2012, 19-year-old North Carolina student Faith Hedgepeth was found murdered in her apartment; 14 years later, DNA evidence helped convict a man, who received life in prison without parole
articles.summary: Faith Hedgepeth's tragic murder case concludes with Miguel Salguero Olivares receiving a life sentence without parole, following pivotal DNA evidence linking him to the crime, 14 years after her brutal death.
articles.body: A man has been sentenced to life in prison without parole for the 2012 murder of University of North Carolina student Faith Hedgepeth, ending a case that remained unsolved for nearly a decade before DNA evidence led investigators to a suspect.Miguel Salguero Olivares, 33, was convicted on Friday of first-degree murder, rape, sexual offence and burglary. He was arrested in 2021 after a DNA sample collected during a driving-under-the-influence stop allegedly matched evidence recovered from the crime scene.Jurors deliberated for six hours over two days before reaching their verdict. Along with the life sentence for murder, Salguero Olivares received an additional 45 to 65 years in prison for the other offences.Hedgepeth was 19 and a sophomore at the university when she was found beaten to death in her off-campus apartment in September 2012. Prosecutors presented DNA, fingerprint and palm-print evidence linking Salguero Olivares to the crime.DNA evidence formed the centre of the prosecutionProsecutors said Salguero Olivares' DNA was found in Hedgepeth's body, on a note written on a fast-food bag and on a blood-covered rum bottle identified as the murder weapon. His fingerprints and palm print were also linked to evidence recovered at the scene.Forensic scientist Erin Ermish testified that the DNA recovered from Hedgepeth's body was 170 septillion times more likely to have come from a mixture of Hedgepeth's DNA and Salguero Olivares' than from Hedgepeth and an unidentified person.Ermish also told the court that DNA recovered from the top of the rum bottle was 48.6 tredecillion times more likely to have come from Hedgepeth and Salguero Olivares than from two unrelated, unidentified people.The prosecution argued that the forensic findings provided compelling evidence of Salguero Olivares' involvement."We know who did it. The forensic evidence is screaming his name," prosecutor Angela Garcia-Lamarca said during closing arguments, as per the AP.Defence challenges investigation and forensic findingsSalguero Olivares' lawyers argued that investigators had focused on their client prematurely and failed to examine other possibilities. They questioned how evidence was handled, the processing of the apartment and the reliability of parts of the DNA analysis.The defence also challenged the account of Hedgepeth's roommate, Karena Rosario, who said she had left the apartment after returning from a night out and came back hours later to find Hedgepeth's body.Lawyers argued that investigators had failed to search some areas of the apartment and had subsequently lost some potential blood evidence. They also noted that DNA from sexual intercourse can remain in the body for days, challenging the prosecution's interpretation of the biological evidence.Defence attorney Jason Murphy suggested that a prior sexual encounter between Salguero Olivares and Hedgepeth could explain some of the DNA evidence. He also accused investigators of having "tunnel vision" in pursuing the case.The prosecution rejected those arguments, maintaining that the forensic evidence remained significant despite acknowledged investigative shortcomings."No matter what kind of mistakes were made or things that were missed, it doesn’t erase the palm print; it doesn’t somehow lift the DNA out of Faith," special prosecutor Lisa Coltrane said.What happened the night Hedgepeth diedHedgepeth was found dead in her apartment after a night out on September 7, 2012. Rosario testified that she had been drunk and unwell when Hedgepeth drove them home from a club at about 2am. Rosario later called a friend to collect her, leaving Hedgepeth alone in the apartment. She returned several hours later and discovered her roommate's body.An autopsy found extensive fractures to Hedgepeth's skull, cuts to her face and head, and injuries to her arms and legs.Prosecutors suggested that Salguero Olivares may have attended a barbecue at a neighbour's home that night, attempted to approach the young women in the parking lot and returned after Rosario left. However, no witness corroborated that account. Garcia-Lamarca told jurors they did not need to accept that theory to find him guilty.Salguero Olivares did not testify during the trial, and the defence rested without calling witnesses.Hedgepeth's parents forgive her killerFollowing the verdict and sentencing, Hedgepeth's parents told the court that they forgave the man convicted of killing their daughter.Her mother, Connie Hedgepeth, said she had reached that decision weeks after her daughter's death, while acknowledging the lasting pain of the loss."It was just three weeks after her death. It didn’t matter who did it, I knew that I had to forgive, and I do forgive, but my heart aches for his family," she said.Her father, Roland Hedgepeth, also addressed the court."Today it got very real," he said. "Nevertheless, I say it without reservation, I forgive Miguel for what he did."You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Trump says he needs to 'stop killing Iranian leaders' to find someone to negotiate with
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has said that he needs to \"stop killing Iranian leaders\" to figure out with whom Washington can negotiate with, while
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has said that he needs to "stop killing Iranian leaders" to figure out with whom Washington can negotiate with, while reiterating that Tehran must never be allowed to develop nuclear weapons.Speaking at a campaign rally in Georgia, Trump claimed that Iran had lost its top leaders and military capabilities, making it difficult for the US to find anyone with whom to negotiate.“I gotta stop” killing Iranian leaders, Trump told the rally, “because I gotta figure out who the hell we're negotiating with.”“They don't have any airplanes, no ships, no anything, no leaders. Level one leader is gone, level two leader is gone,” he added, reiterating his claims about the destruction of Iran's military and leadership.Trump also defended his 2018 decision to withdraw the US from the 2015 Iran nuclear deal, formally known as the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA), which was negotiated under former president Barack Obama.“We obliterated Iran's nuclear enrichment capacity with Operation Midnight Hammer and Operation Epic Fury,” Trump said, referring to US military operations in 2025 and between February and May this year.“We defeated them militarily, financially, and otherwise. We have to make sure that they never, ever have a nuclear weapon,” he added.Trump had earlier indicated that the US could launch another attack on Iran, while also leaving open the possibility of reaching an agreement with Tehran.Speaking to reporters after casting his ballot in the midterm elections in Florida early on Saturday, Trump was asked whether the US would carry out a possible attack on Iran."Do you really think I'd tell you that? Maybe tomorrow...There's a possibility I will. There's also a possibility we'll have a nice, big, beautiful agreement. They want to make a deal, but the problem is, will they hold the deal?" he said.The US president also praised the American military's role in the conflict and defended his administration's approach to West Asia."We have done an amazing job. Our Navy and military have done an amazing job. They have knocked out every jet fighter of Iran. 259 ships are at the bottom of the sea. They are only left with record inflation," he added.Later on Sunday, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf accused Washington of pushing itself into a crisis through miscalculations and its decision to wage war against Iran. He said the responsibility for resolving the confrontation rested with the US.According to remarks reported by Iranian news agency ISNA, Ghalibaf said Tehran had nothing new to add to its position."As I have also stated previously, we have nothing new to say. It was America that, through miscalculations and waging war against Iran, stepped into a quagmire, and it is now they who must take the necessary measures to rescue themselves," he said during a parliamentary session in Tehran.Ghalibaf rejected the suggestion that military threats or media pressure would force Iran to surrender."The Americans assume that with a few levers of media pressure or military threats, they can make this great nation surrender to them, unaware that today's Iran is not the Iran of the humiliating Pahlavi era, but rather a strong fortress of self-confidence, defensive capability, and iron will that will never allow any foreign power to dictate terms to the honour of this land," he said."We will not be intimidated, and we are prepared to deliver a response beyond their imagination to any violation of the territorial integrity of great Iran," Ghalibaf said. "Therefore, threats of widespread war or assassination are not matters that will make the Iranian nation compromise on its rights and interests."He added that diplomatic statements from Washington would carry little weight without a change in policy and concrete steps to address past commitments."Until the Americans change their behaviour, abandon their bullying nature and greed, and make tangible, concrete, and real amends on the ground for their violated commitments, no claim will hold a shred of credibility for the Islamic Republic of Iran," he said.Meanwhile, Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran's policies would remain unchanged regardless of whether another war broke out. He warned that any further military action against Iran would be irrational.Araghchi also said the Strait of Hormuz would not return to its previous state following the 40-day war, arguing that the conflict had fundamentally changed the regional security landscape.You use AI every day. articles.title: Shardul Thakur injury update: Mumbai all-rounder to miss Haryana Ranji Trophy match
articles.summary: Mumbai's experienced all-rounder Shardul Thakur will not participate in the upcoming match against Haryana due to a finger injury. The team has made a strong...
articles.body:
Mumbai's bid to extend their winning run in the Ranji Trophy will have to continue without the services of experienced all-rounder Shardul Thakur, who remains short of full fitness following a finger injury. Mumbai have made a dominant start to their campaign, but will be without one of their key players when they take on Haryana in an Elite Group D clash at the BKC Complex from Monday. Thakur has been sidelined since sustaining the injury during a training session ahead of the season's opening round. Although the 34-year-old has resumed training with the Mumbai squad, he has yet to regain full match fitness. He was initially expected to miss at least the first two rounds, with the team hopeful of having him available for the Haryana fixture.

Mumbai decide against rushing Thakur's return

Mumbai have decided against rushing Thakur back into action and are set to field the same squad that secured a comprehensive victory over Himachal Pradesh in Bilaspur in their previous outing, according to cricinfo. Thakur last featured in the Duleep Trophy quarter-final for West Zone against North Zone in late August. He bowled 14 overs, picked up one wicket and scored 10 runs in his only innings as West Zone suffered a 54-run defeat. While continuing his recovery and working towards a return to competitive cricket, Thakur is also set to take up commentary duties for some of India's ongoing T20 Internationals against New Zealand.

Mumbai ride on dominant start to Ranji campaign

Mumbai have made an impressive start to their Ranji Trophy campaign, registering consecutive innings victories to collect 14 points and move to the top of Elite Group D. They began with an innings-and-155-run win over Chandigarh at the Wankhede Stadium before defeating Himachal Pradesh by an innings and 97 runs in Bilaspur. Mumbai will look to maintain that momentum as they prepare for a tougher challenge against another in-form side.

Mumbai will also be without vice-captain Ayush Mhatre, who is recovering from a hamstring injury, while opener Yashasvi Jaiswal is in New Zealand ahead of the upcoming Test series after featuring in the India A series. Haryana, meanwhile, have also won their opening two matches, setting up a meeting between the top two teams in Elite Group D.

articles.summary: Nine amusement ride workers stranded by a sudden Vellar river surge in Perambalur were rescued with ropes; inflow hit 40,000 cusecs after upstream rain.
articles.body: Trichy: Nine workers who were stranded after dismantling amusement rides on the Vellar riverbed in Perambalur district following a sudden increase in water flow were rescued by fire and rescue services personnel on Sunday.Fire service personnel said the nine from Salem had completed dismantling joy rides such as giant wheel on Saturday night as the exhibition in Labbaikudikadu had got over last week. The workers then slept on the riverbank on Saturday night.
